title: String Compression III
statement:
Compress the string `word` into a new string `comp`, which starts out empty. As long as `word` still has characters, look at its first character `c` and cut off the longest prefix that consists only of `c` and is at most 9 characters long. Append that prefix's length (a single digit from 1 to 9) followed by `c` to `comp`.

Return `comp` once all of `word` has been used up.
constraints: word contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The rule only ever looks at the front of what is left of `word`, so one left-to-right scan is enough: measure the run of equal letters at the current position, but stop counting at 9, because a block's length has to be a single digit. A longer run simply turns into several blocks of the same letter, so 14 a's become `9a` and then `5a`. Collecting the blocks in a list and joining them once at the end avoids copying a growing string again and again.

## Approach

1. Keep `parts`, the output blocks, and `i`, the position of the next unread character.
2. While `i` is inside `word`, take `letter = word[i]` and start `run` at 0.
3. Move `i` forward while it still points at `letter` and `run < 9`, counting the steps in `run`.
4. Push `run` followed by `letter` onto `parts`. The next block starts at the new `i`, even when it is the same letter.
5. Return `parts.join('')`.

## Example 1, step by step

`word = "abcde"`. At `i = 0`, `letter = "a"` and the inner loop stops after one step because `word[1]` is `"b"`, so `"1a"` is pushed and `i = 1`. The same happens for `b`, `c`, `d` and `e`, and joining the parts gives `"1a1b1c1d1e"`. In Example 2 the cap matters: the inner loop stops at `run = 9` inside the 14 a's, so `"9a"` is pushed, then `"5a"` and `"2b"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is read once by the inner loop.
- Space: O(n) for the output, which is at most twice as long as `word`.

## Pitfalls

- Cap every block at 9: ten a's give `"9a1a"`, never `"10a"`.
- After a capped block the next block may use the same letter; do not merge or skip it.
- Adding to a string in a loop can copy the whole string each time (Java's `String +=`); use a `StringBuilder` in Java and a buffer of `2 * n + 1` characters in C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parts` | the compressed blocks, joined at the end |
| `i` | position of the next unread character of `word` |
| `letter` | the character of the current block |
| `run` | the current block's length, at most 9 |

narration.2: The compressed blocks are collected here and joined once at the end.
narration.3: i is the position of the next character that has not been compressed yet.
narration.5: Keep making blocks until the whole word has been read.
narration.6: The new block is made of the letter at i.
narration.7: No characters have been counted for this block yet.
narration.8: Extend the block while the letter repeats, but never past 9 characters.
narration.9: Count one more copy of the letter...
narration.12: Record the block as its length digit followed by its letter.
narration.14: Join the blocks into the compressed string.
